sections.heading: The physics toolkit
bullets: Power = voltage × current: a megawatt is 2,500A at 400V or 1,250A at 800V — same power, very different copper
Conductor loss scales with the SQUARE of current (I²R): double the voltage, quarter the loss — every architecture decision is ultimately a voltage decision
Every conversion stage costs ~1–3% as heat (paid again in cooling), a box of capex and floor space, and a failure mode — architecture design is the art of deleting stages
The grid is AC because transformers only work on AC; chips, batteries and solar are all DC-native — every AC segment between a battery and a chip is historical, not physical

sections.heading: The Western AC chain (the incumbent)
bullets: Transmission (115–345kVac) → substation (12.47–34.5kVac in the US) → MV transformer (480Vac US / 400Vac international) → UPS → PDU transformer → server PSU (54Vdc) → VRMs (~1V at the die)
The double-conversion UPS secretly rectifies AC to DC for its battery, then inverts back to AC — the chain converts to DC twice and throws it away once
Seven to eight series stages; end-to-end efficiency roughly 88–94%
It persists because it is inherited: UL/NEC codes, AC-trained field labor, and fifty years of UPS/PDU vendor incumbency

sections.heading: China's HVDC: 240V/336V DC (Zhonhen's franchise)
bullets: Descended from telecom −48Vdc battery plants: rectify once, float the battery directly on the bus, zero transfer time — no UPS, no inverter, no transfer switch
The adoption trick: a stock server PSU's universal input accepts 240Vdc without modification — China's DC transition required no server changes at all
Chain: 10kVac → 380Vac → HVDC rectifier (240/336Vdc, ≥97.5%) with batteries on the bus → DC distribution → stock PSU → chip. About five stages against the AC chain's eight
336Vdc adds headroom and efficiency but needs DC-rated PSUs — used where operators control the hardware fleet
Zhonhen shipped the first-generation 240Vdc system (2010) and lead-drafted the national 240V/336V standard; independently ranked #1 in China data-center HVDC at 31% share (2025)

sections.heading: Panama power: medium voltage to DC in one stage
bullets: Folds the MV transformer, rectification and distribution into ONE factory-built, pre-tested module: 10kVac in → 240/400/800Vdc out, >97.5% system efficiency, 2.5MW blocks
Named like the canal — one cut instead of four locks; co-developed with Alibaba (2019)
In NVIDIA-ecosystem vocabulary its device class is the solid-state transformer / MV rectifier 'sidecar'
Prefabrication moves DC arc-management engineering into the factory — and substitutes factory labor for scarce field electricians

sections.heading: 800Vdc: the West arrives at the same thesis
bullets: AI racks (120–150kW today, ~600kW Kyber-class 2H 2027, 1MW beyond) physically break AC-to-the-rack: a legacy 1MW rack needs ~200kg of busbar
NVIDIA's architecture: 13.8kVac → SST/MV rectifier sidecar → 800Vdc bus → in-rack DC/DC → ~0.8V; supercaps and battery shelves hang on the DC bus
NVIDIA's published numbers: +157% power through the same copper vs 415Vac, −45% copper, ~+5% end-to-end efficiency, ~30% lower TCO
Why 800V: I²R at megawatt-rack power, plus the EV industry already made 800V-class components cheap

The convergence line: China standardized DC-to-the-rack in 2010 because 240Vdc rides through a stock PSU; NVIDIA is standardizing 800Vdc because AI racks broke AC — same thesis, voltage scaled to the load

sections.heading: DC safety literacy
bullets: An AC arc self-extinguishes 120 times a second at zero crossings; a DC arc has no zero crossing and must be engineered out: DC-rated breakers, arc-fault management, grounding design
Solved at 240/336V across a decade of Chinese fleet operations; the 800V ecosystem is doing the same engineering now

flashcards.q: Why does doubling distribution voltage cut conductor loss to a quarter?
flashcards.a: Loss = I²R. Same power at double the voltage means half the current, and loss scales with current squared: (½)² = ¼.

flashcards.q: Where does DC secretly appear inside the conventional AC chain?
flashcards.a: Twice: inside the double-conversion UPS (rectified for the battery, then inverted back to AC) and after the server PSU. The chain makes DC twice and throws it away once.

flashcards.q: What made 240Vdc adoptable in China without changing any servers?
flashcards.a: A stock server PSU's universal input (90–264Vac) rectifies immediately at its front end — feed it 240Vdc and it passes through. The IT fleet ran unmodified.

flashcards.q: Why does an HVDC plant need no transfer switch or inverter?
flashcards.a: Battery strings float directly on the DC bus. When the grid fails, nothing switches — the bus simply drains the battery. Zero transfer time.

flashcards.q: What is a Panama power module in one sentence?
flashcards.a: Medium voltage to DC in one factory-built stage: 10kVac in, 240/400/800Vdc out, >97.5% efficiency, ~2.5MW per pre-tested block — the device class NVIDIA's ecosystem calls an SST or MV sidecar.

flashcards.q: Count the stages: conventional AC chain vs 240Vdc HVDC vs Panama.
flashcards.a: Roughly 7–8 (three transformers + UPS's two conversions + PSU + VRMs) vs ~5 (rectify once, battery on bus) vs ~3 (grid → module → rack).

flashcards.q: Why is NVIDIA's number 800V and not 240V?
flashcards.a: I²R at megawatt-rack power — 800V carries an AI rack at a quarter of 400V's conductor loss — plus the EV industry already made 800V-class semiconductors, cables and connectors cheap.

flashcards.q: What are NVIDIA's published gains for 800Vdc vs 415Vac?
flashcards.a: About 157% more power through the same copper, up to 45% less copper, ~5% better end-to-end efficiency, ~30% lower TCO.

flashcards.q: What is DC's one genuine safety disadvantage, and its answer?
flashcards.a: A DC arc has no zero crossing so it doesn't self-extinguish. Answer: DC-rated breakers, arc-fault management and grounding design — solved at fleet scale at 240/336V, being engineered now at 800V.

flashcards.q: What's the difference between 336Vdc and 240Vdc systems?
flashcards.a: 336V lowers current further (thinner copper, slightly better efficiency) but exceeds stock-PSU passthrough tolerance, so it needs DC-rated supplies — used where the operator controls the fleet.

flashcards.q: What does 'HVDC' mean in the data-center context vs the grid context?
flashcards.a: In data centers: 240/336/800Vdc distribution inside the facility ('high' relative to telecom −48V). On the grid: ±hundreds-of-kV transmission. Same acronym, unrelated products.

flashcards.q: Why did DC win in China first — physics or institutions?
flashcards.a: Institutions. A few hyperscalers and three operators who own their fleets could standardize by fiat, and 240Vdc needed no server changes. The US had UL/NEC codes, AC-trained labor and thousands of buyers. AI density is what forces the US hand now.
